description: H2Integrate models hybrid plants producing electricity, hydrogen and industrial products. Its Python package includes equipment models, location-dependent resources, user-selected costs and scenario or design optimisation. The provider is National Laboratory of the Rockies and H2Integrate contributors. Coverage: The software is generic, not a measured geographic dataset. Spatial detail and simulation periods are supplied by the user. Access: The public source repository provides documentation and installation instructions. Source archives and dependencies were not downloaded or run. Licence and cost: The repository identifies BSD-3-Clause and a stable package distribution. Input datasets and dependencies may carry separate conditions. Limitations: The project was previously called GreenHEART. Equipment-model coverage and reported publications do not establish accuracy for every technology. For simulation it supports plant configuration and techno-economic comparisons across generation, storage and conversion technologies. Related resources: model-urbanopt-sdk provides separate district-scale energy modelling. No direct coupling was established.
